source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = wages 30,000.00 + Roth conversion 20,000.00 = 50,000.00. Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 32,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 50,000.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70): yes; question 2 federal AGI 50,000.00 less than or equal to 107,000.00: yes. Table: person 0 line 2 0.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 0.00; line 4 = 0.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 0.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 0.00 = 0.00; RI-1040 line 2 = 0.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 50,000.00 + (0.00) = 50,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 50,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Single). Line 5 = 50,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 39,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 39,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 34,000.00. Line 8 tax on 34,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 34,000.00 x 0.0375 = 1275.000000 = 1,275.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 1,275.00. Note: The sources do not say where a conversion falls, so the projection leaves it out of the modification; it stays taxed.
accepted_approximations: Roth conversions are left out of the pension and annuity modification; the sources do not say where a conversion falls (covers_unclear).
